subject: Mixed (Real Weightage)
description: 100 questions following the real PGP-CET 2025 subject weightage. Mix: 0 easy / 100 medium / 0 hard. Tier is relative: the medium third of the 60 papers by average question difficulty. Every question cites its source.

questions.question: For a diagnosis of Generalised Anxiety Disorder (GAD), the symptoms of anxiety should have persisted for at least:
questions.explanation: Generalised Anxiety Disorder requires anxiety symptoms to have lasted for at least 6 months, with an insidious onset typically in the third decade and a stable, usually chronic course.
questions.sourceBook: Ahuja, A Short Textbook of Psychiatry
questions.sourceChapter: Neurotic, Stress-related and Somatoform Disorders — Anxiety Disorder
questions.subject: Psychiatry

questions.question: Rheumatoid arthritis is most strongly associated with:
questions.explanation: HLA-DR4 (and DR1) carries risk for seropositive rheumatoid arthritis; HLA-B27 is for seronegative spondyloarthropathies.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: In a normal distribution, approximately what percentage of values lie within ±1 SD of the mean?
questions.explanation: 68% within ±1 SD, 95% within ±1.96 (≈2) SD, 99.7% within ±3 SD.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: Sensations of touch, pain, and pressure (somatosensory input) arrive at the region of the cortex located:

options.B: In the parietal lobe, on the gyrus immediately behind the central sulcus
options.C: In the temporal lobe, buried in the lateral fissure
options.D: Only in the cerebellum, never the cerebrum

questions.explanation: Somatosensory signals (touch, pain, pressure) reach the primary somatosensory cortex, located in the parietal lobe on the gyrus immediately behind the central sulcus — right next to the primary motor cortex, which lies on the gyrus just in front of the central sulcus.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology
questions.sourceChapter: Biology of Behavior — Sensory and Motor Functions
questions.subject: Psychology

questions.question: The Q-angle of the knee is formed by:

options.B: A line from the ASIS to the centre of the patella and a line from the patella to the tibial tubercle

questions.explanation: Normal Q-angle is about 13° in men and 18° in women; larger values predispose to patellar maltracking.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: A fracture of the shaft of the humerus most commonly injures the:
questions.explanation: In the spiral groove.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: Which is NOT a subphase of the stance phase?
questions.explanation: Stance: initial contact, loading response, mid-stance, terminal stance, pre-swing. Swing: initial, mid, terminal swing.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: Cortisol secretion shows a diurnal rhythm with the peak at:
questions.explanation: It increases blood glucose, suppresses inflammation and mobilises protein.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: Which factor would NOT normally invalidate a manual muscle test?

options.B: Poor patient understanding of the command
options.C: Testing in the standard position with proper stabilisation

questions.explanation: Pain, substitution and misunderstanding reduce reliability; correct positioning and stabilisation increase it.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: The lateral intermuscular septum of the thigh, the thickest of the three septa, separates which two compartments?

options.A: The anterior compartment from the posterior compartment
options.B: The medial compartment from the posterior compartment
options.C: The anterior compartment from the medial compartment
options.D: It does not separate any compartments

questions.explanation: The lateral intermuscular septum, the thickest of the thigh's three intermuscular septa, extends from the iliotibial tract to the lateral lip of the linea aspera and separates the anterior compartment of the thigh from the posterior compartment.
questions.sourceBook: BD Chaurasia's Human Anatomy — Lower Limb
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: The 'unpacking principle' in clinical reasoning refers to the risk that:

options.A: A failure to fully take the history and examine the patient means important information can be missed, leading to error
options.B: Patients should always be admitted for observation regardless of findings
options.C: Clinical prediction rules should never be used
options.D: Diagnostic tests are always more reliable than clinical examination

questions.explanation: The unpacking principle highlights that history-taking and physical examination, though seemingly obvious steps, are sometimes performed inadequately — and this failure to 'unpack' all the available information can cause important findings to be missed.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine
questions.sourceChapter: Clinical Decision Making — Reducing Errors, Cognitive Debiasing Strategies
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: The maximum predicted heart rate in a healthy adult is commonly estimated as:
questions.explanation: A 40-year-old: 180 bpm. Moderate intensity is ~64–76% of HRmax.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Unilateral spatial neglect following stroke is most commonly associated with a lesion of the:
questions.explanation: Right parietal damage leads to inattention to the left side of space despite intact sensation and vision.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: The normal arterial PaO2 in a healthy adult breathing room air is approximately:
questions.explanation: PaO2 <60 mmHg (8 kPa) defines type 1 respiratory failure; normal PaCO2 is 35–45 mmHg.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: An 'obstructive' spirometry pattern is characterised by:

options.A: Reduction in FEV1 with relative preservation of FVC (forced vital capacity)
options.B: Simultaneous reduction of both FEV1 and FVC with an increased FEV1/FVC ratio
options.C: No change in either FEV1 or FVC
options.D: An increase in both FEV1 and FVC

questions.explanation: An obstructive pattern shows a reduction in FEV1 (forced expiratory volume in 1 second) with relative preservation of FVC, lowering the FEV1/FVC ratio — this indicates airway obstruction, graded by severity (e.g. <75% mild, <60% moderate, <40% severe). A restrictive pattern, by contrast, shows simultaneous reduction of both FEV1 and FVC with an increased ratio.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: The myotome tested by resisted ankle dorsiflexion is:
questions.explanation: Myotomes: L2 hip flexion, L3 knee extension, L4 ankle dorsiflexion, L5 great toe extension, S1 plantar flexion/eversion.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: Which is a major criterion in the Jones criteria for rheumatic fever?

options.B: Carditis, migratory polyarthritis, chorea, erythema marginatum and subcutaneous nodules

questions.explanation: Minor criteria: fever, arthralgia, raised acute phase reactants, prolonged PR interval.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.topic: Electrical Stimulation of Nerve and Muscle
questions.question: When faradic-type current is applied directly over an innervated muscle, maximum contraction response is generally obtained by stimulating at the:

options.B: Motor point — where the main nerve enters the muscle (or, for deep muscles, where it emerges from under more superficial muscles)
options.C: Muscle belly midpoint, regardless of nerve entry

questions.explanation: The motor point — the point at which the main nerve supply enters the muscle, or for deeply placed muscles, the point where the nerve emerges from under overlying superficial muscles — is where maximum contraction response is typically obtained with electrical stimulation.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy
questions.sourceChapter: Electrical Stimulation of Nerve and Muscle — Effects of Nerve Stimulation
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Lenz's law states that:

options.A: Radiation intensity falls with the square of the distance
options.B: An induced EMF acts in a direction that opposes the change producing it
options.D: Heat produced is proportional to current squared

questions.explanation: The induced EMF always opposes the change in magnetic flux that causes it — the basis of self-inductance in coils and choke coils.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: A Venturi mask delivers:

options.C: A fixed, accurate concentration of oxygen irrespective of the patient's breathing pattern

questions.explanation: A high-flow device using entrainment of air through colour-coded valves.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: The energy value of one gram of fat is:
questions.explanation: Carbohydrate 4, protein 4, fat 9, alcohol 7 kcal per gram.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: The talar tilt (inversion stress) test assesses the integrity of the:
questions.explanation: The anterior drawer test examines ATFL; the talar tilt (inversion) tests the CFL. Eversion stress tests the deltoid.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Aerobic training mainly improves:

options.C: Maximal oxygen uptake (VO2 max) and cardiovascular endurance

questions.explanation: Training adaptations include increased stroke volume, capillary density and mitochondrial enzymes.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: In PUVA therapy for psoriasis, UVA irradiation is given:

options.B: At the same time as an X-ray

questions.explanation: Psoralen photosensitises the skin; UVA is then given about 2 hours after ingestion. Eye protection (UV-blocking glasses) is needed for many hours afterwards.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: If a patient's active range is less than passive range at the knee, the most likely cause is:
questions.explanation: When PROM is greater than AROM the limitation is in the contractile unit; when both are equally limited the joint structures are restricted.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: Blastomas (embryomas) such as neuroblastoma, nephroblastoma (Wilms' tumour), and retinoblastoma are notable because they:

options.A: Occur almost exclusively in adults over 60
options.B: Arise from embryonal/partially differentiated cells and occur more frequently in infants and children under 5
options.C: Are always benign despite the '-oma' name

questions.explanation: Blastomas arise from embryonal or partially differentiated cells that would normally form the blastema of organs/tissues during embryogenesis, and occur more frequently in infants and children under 5 years of age.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: Parathyroid hormone (PTH) acts to:

options.C: Raise plasma calcium by increasing bone resorption and renal reabsorption and activating vitamin D

questions.explanation: Calcitonin lowers plasma calcium.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: Adson's test is positive when:

options.A: The radial pulse diminishes with the neck extended and rotated toward the tested side with deep inspiration (thoracic outlet syndrome)
options.D: The hand tingles on percussion of the median nerve

questions.explanation: Adson's test checks for scalene compression of the subclavian artery; roos and Wright tests are also used.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: The phrenic nerve, supplying the diaphragm, arises from segments:
questions.explanation: ‘C3, 4, 5 keeps the diaphragm alive’: lesions above C3 need ventilatory support.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Chorea, dementia and an autosomal dominant inheritance are features of:
questions.explanation: Degeneration of the caudate nucleus; CAG repeat expansion on chromosome 4.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: The minimal erythema dose (first-degree erythema, E1) is the:

options.A: Dose that has no effect at all
options.B: Smallest UV exposure that produces just-visible reddening of the skin after the latent period
options.D: Dose that causes immediate tanning only

questions.explanation: E1 is the threshold dose. E2 ≈ 2.5 × E1 (bright red, peeling), E3 ≈ 5 × E1 (painful with blisters/oedema), E4 ≈ 10 × E1 (severe blistering).
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: During galvanic (direct) current application, excitability of the nerve is increased beneath the:
questions.explanation: The cathode partially depolarises the nerve, increasing excitability (catelectrotonus). The anode hyperpolarises and reduces excitability (anelectrotonus).
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Which of the following can NOT be used as a substrate for gluconeogenesis?
questions.explanation: Even-chain fatty acids cannot be converted to glucose in humans.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Biochemistry

questions.question: Which muscle prevents winging of the scapula?
questions.explanation: Serratus anterior holds the scapula against the thoracic wall.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: For measuring elbow flexion with a universal goniometer, the axis is placed over the:
questions.explanation: Fixed arm along the humerus toward the acromion, moving arm along the radius toward the radial styloid, axis at the lateral epicondyle.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: Which feature is NOT a sign of chronic liver disease?
questions.explanation: Chronic liver disease: spider naevi, palmar erythema, clubbing, leuconychia, ascites, gynaecomastia. Koilonychia suggests iron deficiency.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: Prone lying for 30 minutes several times a day is of particular importance after which amputation?
questions.explanation: Prone lying stretches the hip flexors and helps prevent hip flexion contracture, which would prevent a good prosthetic gait.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: In the Rancho Los Amigos Scale, level IV is characterised by:
questions.explanation: I no response; II generalised; III localised; IV confused-agitated; V confused-inappropriate; VI confused-appropriate; VII automatic-appropriate; VIII purposeful.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: 'Overconfidence bias' in clinical decision-making refers to:

options.A: The tendency to always order more diagnostic tests than necessary
options.B: The tendency to believe one knows more than one actually does, placing too much faith in opinion over gathered evidence
options.C: A bias that only affects junior doctors, never senior clinicians
options.D: Excessive reliance on clinical prediction rules

questions.explanation: Overconfidence bias is the tendency to place too much faith in one's own opinion rather than the gathered evidence, sometimes compounded further by availability bias and commission bias (a tendency to act rather than not act), occasionally with serious consequences.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine
questions.sourceChapter: Clinical Decision Making — Common Cognitive Biases
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: Middle Cerebral Artery (MCA) syndrome, the most common site of occlusion in stroke, classically produces contralateral weakness and sensory loss most affecting:

options.A: The lower extremity, sparing the face and upper extremity
options.B: The face and upper extremity, with relative sparing of the lower extremity

questions.explanation: MCA syndrome classically produces contralateral spastic hemiparesis and sensory loss of the face, upper extremity, and lower extremity, with the face and upper extremity more affected than the lower extremity — the MCA is also the most common site of stroke occlusion overall.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan, Physical Rehabilitation
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 15: Stroke — Middle Cerebral Artery Syndrome
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Poliovirus belongs to which group?
questions.explanation: Faecal–oral transmission; oral vaccine (Sabin) is a live attenuated vaccine.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: Weakness of serratus anterior is best demonstrated by:

options.A: Winging of the scapula when the arm is pushed forward against resistance
options.B: Inability to abduct the arm past 90° only
options.C: Loss of sensation in the deltoid area

questions.explanation: Long thoracic nerve palsy causes medial border winging on forward pushing or wall push-up.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: The Oxford technique of progressive resistive exercise differs from DeLorme's in that:

options.A: The lightest set is performed first
options.C: The heaviest set is performed first and the load is reduced in successive sets

questions.explanation: Oxford (Zinovieff): 100%, 75%, 50% of 10-RM so that load decreases as the muscle fatigues.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: HbA1c reflects average blood glucose over about:
questions.explanation: Reflects glycation of haemoglobin over the 120-day red cell lifespan.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: Which statement about peripheral nerve fibres is correct?

options.A: Conduction velocity is unrelated to fibre diameter
options.B: Unmyelinated C fibres conduct faster than A fibres
options.C: Small-diameter fibres have the lowest threshold to electrical stimulation
options.D: Large-diameter myelinated fibres conduct fastest and have the lowest stimulation threshold

questions.explanation: Large myelinated fibres (Aα/Aβ) are excited first and conduct fastest. This is why sensory TENS and motor stimulation can be selectively recruited before pain fibres.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Prolonged bed rest produces which cardiovascular effect?

options.D: Orthostatic hypotension and decreased stroke volume

questions.explanation: Deconditioning leads to a loss of plasma volume (~10% in a week) and reduced exercise capacity.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Activation of a Gi-coupled receptor typically has which effect on adenylyl cyclase and cAMP?

options.C: Has no effect on adenylyl cyclase, acts only on phospholipase C

questions.explanation: Gi (inhibitory G-protein) inhibits adenylyl cyclase, lowering intracellular cAMP — the opposite of Gs, which activates adenylyl cyclase and raises cAMP. This is why, for example, muscarinic M2 receptor stimulation (Gi-coupled) in the heart opposes the effect of beta-adrenergic (Gs-coupled) stimulation.
questions.sourceBook: KD Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology
questions.sourceChapter: Mechanism of Drug Action; Receptor Pharmacology
questions.subject: Pharmacology

questions.question: The most common source of pulmonary embolism is:

options.D: Deep veins of the lower limb

questions.explanation: Deep vein thrombosis of the calf or iliofemoral veins.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: The commonest site of osteosarcoma is the:

options.C: Metaphysis around the knee (distal femur/proximal tibia)

questions.explanation: Peak incidence is in adolescents; pulmonary metastasis via blood is common.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: When bandaging a transfemoral residual limb, the bandage should:

options.A: Be applied only horizontally across the limb
options.B: Apply greater pressure distally than proximally using diagonal turns, without wrinkles
options.C: Avoid including the hip joint in a figure-of-eight
options.D: Apply more pressure proximally than distally

questions.explanation: Distal pressure shapes the limb and reduces oedema; proximal tourniquet effect must be avoided. Wrinkles and circular constriction cause pressure sores.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Which structure is NOT commonly associated with posterior dislocation of the elbow?
questions.explanation: Myositis ossificans traumatica (not progressiva) can complicate an elbow injury.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: In the ICIDH model, difficulty in performing an activity such as walking due to an impairment is termed:
questions.explanation: Impairment (organ level) → disability (person level) → handicap (social level).
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: A competitive antagonist:

options.B: Binds reversibly to the receptor, and its effect can be overcome by increasing the agonist concentration

questions.explanation: Atropine at muscarinic receptors is a competitive antagonist.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Pharmacology

questions.question: In epidemiological studies, 'comparability' between study and control groups is best ensured by:

options.A: Choosing groups of very different ages and backgrounds to maximise contrast
options.B: Randomization or random allocation, or 'matching' for selected characteristics when random allocation is not possible (e.g. case-control/cohort studies)
options.C: Always excluding any consideration of age or sex
options.D: Comparability is not actually necessary for valid epidemiological conclusions

questions.explanation: Comparability ('like being compared with like') between study and control groups is best ensured by randomization or random allocation. Where this is not possible, such as in case-control or cohort studies, 'matching' for selected characteristics is used instead, and standardization can address a limited number of characteristics like age, sex, and parity.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine
questions.sourceChapter: Principles of Epidemiology and Epidemiologic Methods — Making Comparisons
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: In normal pregnancy, exercise should be avoided in the supine position after the first trimester because of:

options.A: Risk of pelvic girdle pain only
options.D: Compression of the inferior vena cava reducing venous return

questions.explanation: The supine hypotensive syndrome causes dizziness and reduced uteroplacental blood flow; use left lateral tilt.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: In prolonged fasting (beyond 48-72 hours), the central nervous system adapts to using which fuel source as primary, reducing the need for muscle protein breakdown?
questions.explanation: After 48-72 hours of fasting, the CNS adapts to using ketone bodies (produced by hepatic ketogenesis from fatty acids, facilitated by low insulin) as its primary fuel source — this 'fat fuel economy' shift reduces the need for muscle breakdown by up to 55 g per day compared to simple short-term starvation.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery
questions.sourceChapter: Nutrition and Fluid Therapy — Metabolic Response to Starvation
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: Risk factors for uterovaginal prolapse include:

options.B: Multiparity, obesity, chronic cough and menopause

questions.explanation: Pelvic floor exercises are first-line for mild prolapse.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: OBGY

questions.question: The Neer impingement test involves the examiner passively and forcibly elevating the patient's medially-rotated arm in the scapular plane. A positive test (pain) is most indicative of an overuse injury to which structure?

options.A: The supraspinatus muscle (and sometimes the biceps tendon)

questions.explanation: The Neer impingement test causes 'jamming' of the greater tuberosity against the anteroinferior border of the acromion; a positive test (reproducing pain) is indicative of an overuse injury to the supraspinatus muscle, and sometimes the biceps tendon.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 5: Shoulder — Common Shoulder Impingement Tests, Neer Impingement Test
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Which feature is LEAST associated with an acute medial meniscus tear?
questions.explanation: Quadriceps wasting (especially vastus medialis) occurs with meniscal and other knee injuries; hamstring atrophy is not typical.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Two-joint muscles such as the hamstrings and gastrocnemius are typically tested in mid-range rather than at full end-range during manual muscle testing. Why?

options.A: To avoid provoking a stretch reflex
options.B: Mid-range gives these muscles a more mechanically favorable length-tension relationship for the test
options.C: Two-joint muscles cannot generate any force at end range
options.D: It standardizes the time taken for every muscle test

questions.explanation: One-joint muscles are tested at end range for consistency, but two-joint muscles are tested in mid-range, where their length-tension relationship is more favorable — testing them at a mechanical disadvantage would make it hard to distinguish a true Grade 5 from a Grade 4.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels and Worthingham's Muscle Testing, 9th ed.
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 1: Principles of Manual Muscle Testing
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: A dynamic factor contributing to abnormal patellar tracking is:
questions.explanation: Muscle imbalance (weak VMO relative to tight lateral structures) is a dynamic factor; bony shape factors such as a shallow groove are static.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: The primary motor cortex (area 4) lies in the:
questions.explanation: The leg area is on the medial surface, supplied by the ACA.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: Which statement about collagen is correct?

options.A: Collagen fibres resist tensile forces and give tendons and ligaments strength
options.B: Collagen resists compression better than tension
options.C: Type II collagen is found mainly in tendons
options.D: Collagen is elastic and stretches by 100%

questions.explanation: Type I collagen predominates in tendons, ligaments, bone and skin; type II in hyaline cartilage.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: In a muscle immobilised in a shortened position the typical adaptation is:

options.D: Loss of sarcomeres in series, so the muscle becomes shorter

questions.explanation: Muscles adapt to their functional length; immobilised in lengthened position they add sarcomeres.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: Vitamin K is necessary for synthesis of clotting factors:
questions.explanation: Warfarin acts by antagonising vitamin K.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: A knee extends actively 5° beyond neutral and flexes to 60°. The correct recording is:
questions.explanation: Hyperextension is recorded first (5), then 0, then flexion (60). Total range = 65°.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: A positive Trendelenburg sign indicates weakness of the:

options.C: Hip abductors (gluteus medius and minimus) on the stance side

questions.explanation: When standing on the weak leg the pelvis drops on the opposite (swing) side. Causes include superior gluteal nerve injury, hip dislocation or coxa vara.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Early ambulation after an uncomplicated vaginal delivery is encouraged mainly because it:

options.A: Has no measurable benefit but is traditional practice
options.B: Reduces bladder complications and constipation, facilitates uterine drainage, and lessens the risk of puerperal venous thrombosis and embolism
options.D: Prevents postpartum haemorrhage entirely on its own

questions.explanation: Early ambulation after delivery provides a sense of well-being, reduces bladder complications and constipation, facilitates uterine drainage (hastening involution), and importantly lessens the risk of puerperal venous thrombosis and embolism.
questions.sourceBook: Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics
questions.sourceChapter: Normal Puerperium — Management, Rest and Ambulation
questions.subject: OBGY

questions.question: Spontaneous fibrillation potentials and positive sharp waves at rest on EMG, appearing about 2–3 weeks after injury, indicate:
questions.explanation: Denervated muscle fibres become hypersensitive to acetylcholine and fire spontaneously; fibrillations and positive sharp waves are the typical findings at rest.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The Motor Relearning Programme (Carr & Shepherd) focuses on:

options.C: Task-specific practice of functional activities with feedback and elimination of unnecessary muscle activity

questions.explanation: It teaches essential components of tasks such as sitting up, standing, walking and reaching using active practice and feedback.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Anterior pelvic tilt increases:
questions.explanation: Tight hip flexors and weak abdominals increase anterior pelvic tilt.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: Which cardiovascular change is normal in pregnancy?

options.C: Increase in cardiac output by 30–50% and fall in systemic vascular resistance

questions.explanation: Plasma volume increases more than red cell mass (physiological anaemia of pregnancy).
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: OBGY

questions.question: Closed-chain exercise is best described as exercise performed:

options.A: In a nonweight-bearing position with the distal segment moving freely
options.B: In a weight-bearing position where the body moves over a fixed distal segment
options.C: Only using free weights, never body weight

questions.explanation: Closed-chain exercise is performed in a weight-bearing position, where the body moves over a relatively fixed distal segment (e.g. the foot on the ground during a squat). Open-chain exercise, by contrast, is performed nonweight-bearing, with the distal segment (hand or foot) moving freely.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 6: Resistance Exercise — Position for Exercise
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: The basic requirements of good epidemiological measurement include validity, reliability, accuracy, sensitivity, and:

options.D: Simplicity above all else, regardless of accuracy

questions.explanation: The basic requirements of measurement in epidemiology are validity, reliability, accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity — these properties determine how trustworthy and useful a given measurement or test is for epidemiological purposes.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine
questions.sourceChapter: Principles of Epidemiology and Epidemiologic Methods — Basic Measurements in Epidemiology
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: 'Passive flexibility' (passive range of motion) is best described as:

options.A: The degree to which an active muscle contraction moves a joint through its available range
options.B: The degree to which a body segment can be moved through its available range by an external force, without the patient contracting the muscle themselves
options.C: The absolute maximum range any joint could reach under general anesthesia
options.D: A measure of muscular endurance during repeated contractions

questions.explanation: Passive flexibility depends on the extensibility of the muscles and connective tissues crossing a joint. It is a prerequisite for, but does not guarantee, dynamic (active) flexibility — which instead depends on the patient's own active muscle contraction moving the segment.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 4: Stretching for Impaired Mobility — Definition of Terms
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: Buerger-Allen exercises are used in:
questions.explanation: The leg is elevated (vasoconstriction/drain), dependent (vasodilatation), then horizontal, in cycles.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Cavitation in ultrasound refers to the:

options.A: Reflection of the beam from bone
options.D: Formation and oscillation of gas bubbles in tissue fluids

questions.explanation: Stable cavitation (bubbles oscillating) is useful non-thermally; transient (unstable) cavitation, where bubbles collapse, is damaging and must be avoided.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The most important factor maintaining stability of the shoulder joint is the:
questions.explanation: The shallow glenoid and loose capsule favour mobility at the expense of stability.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.topic: Electrical Stimulation of Nerve and Muscle
questions.question: Impulses with a duration of MORE than 10 ms, often termed interrupted (or modified) direct current, are specifically used to stimulate:

options.A: Normal, innervated muscle via the motor nerve
options.B: Denervated muscle, where the muscle fibres must be stimulated directly (no functioning motor nerve)

questions.explanation: Long-duration impulses (>10 ms), termed interrupted or modified direct current, are used for denervated muscles — since there is no functioning motor nerve, the muscle fibres must be stimulated directly, and these impulses are repeated far less frequently than faradic-type currents (e.g. a 100 ms impulse might be repeated only about 30 times per minute).
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy
questions.sourceChapter: Electrical Stimulation of Nerve and Muscle
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Madelung's deformity results from retarded growth of which structure?

options.A: The lower end of the radius
options.B: The upper end of the humerus
options.C: The olecranon process of the ulna

questions.explanation: Madelung's deformity is a dorsal subluxation (displacement) of the lower end of the ulna, caused by retarded growth of the lower end of the radius.
questions.sourceBook: BD Chaurasia's Human Anatomy — Upper Limb
questions.sourceChapter: Bones of the Upper Limb — Clinical Anatomy
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: Dry gangrene is typically caused by:

options.D: Arterial occlusion, as in diabetes or atherosclerosis

questions.explanation: Wet gangrene has superadded infection with putrefaction.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: The capsular pattern of the hip joint is:

options.A: Limitation of flexion, abduction and medial rotation
options.D: Limitation of extension and adduction only

questions.explanation: Hip capsular pattern: flexion, abduction and medial rotation are the most restricted; seen in osteoarthritis.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: Which of the following is a correct characteristic of the peptide bond?

options.A: It is highly flexible and freely rotates
options.B: It is rigid and planar, with partial double-bond character, generally existing in the trans configuration
options.C: It cannot participate in hydrogen bonding
options.D: It only forms between two acidic amino acids

questions.explanation: The peptide bond (C=O to N-H) has partial double-bond character, which makes it rigid and planar rather than freely rotating, and it generally exists in the trans configuration. Both the C=O and N-H groups are polar and participate in hydrogen bond formation, which is important for secondary structure.
questions.sourceBook: Satyanarayana, Biochemistry
questions.sourceChapter: Proteins and Amino Acids — Peptide Bond
questions.subject: Biochemistry

questions.question: Gas gangrene is caused by:
questions.explanation: Characterised by crepitus, foul-smelling discharge and rapid spreading myonecrosis; treated by radical debridement and penicillin.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: Which of the following is a recognised physiotherapy technique to temporarily reduce spasticity?

options.B: Slow, sustained stretch and prolonged cold or neutral warmth

questions.explanation: Slow stretch reduces muscle spindle sensitivity; prolonged cold reduces gamma activity. Quick stretch and tapping facilitate.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: The insulating (spacing) material between the plates of a capacitor is chosen to have:

options.D: A high dielectric constant, which increases the capacitance

questions.explanation: A higher dielectric constant allows a given plate area and spacing to store more charge, i.e. increases capacitance.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: During dynamic exercise, which cardiovascular change occurs?

options.D: Increase in heart rate, stroke volume and systolic blood pressure

questions.explanation: Diastolic pressure remains unchanged or falls slightly due to vasodilatation in muscles.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: Central cord syndrome typically produces:

options.A: Greater weakness in the lower limbs than the upper limbs
options.C: Greater weakness in the upper limbs than the lower limbs
options.D: Complete flaccid paralysis below the lesion

questions.explanation: Hyperextension injuries in older patients with cervical spondylosis; cervical tracts for the arms lie centrally, so the arms are weaker.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: In Paget's disease of bone the serum alkaline phosphatase is typically:
questions.explanation: Also bone pain, deformity (sabre tibia), deafness and risk of osteosarcoma.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: Fluidotherapy is a form of:

options.C: Dry heat using a warm air-suspended bed of fine particles

questions.explanation: Fluidotherapy circulates warm air through finely divided cellulose particles that behave like a fluid, giving dry heat with massage-like stimulation.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.topic: Electrical Stimulation of Nerve and Muscle
questions.question: Impulses with a duration of less than 10 ms, used for stimulating normal (innervated) muscle, are classified as having:

options.A: A long duration, termed interrupted direct current
options.B: A short duration, of the faradic type
options.C: No classification exists for pulse duration
options.D: A duration only used for denervated muscle

questions.explanation: Impulses of less than 10 ms duration are classed as short duration and are of the faradic type, used to stimulate normal innervated muscle via its motor nerve, typically repeated at a high rate of 50-100 per second.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy
questions.sourceChapter: Electrical Stimulation of Nerve and Muscle
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Regarding physical activity and stroke risk, which finding is reported?

options.A: Moderate to vigorous exercise is associated with about a 35% reduction in stroke risk, while light exercise (walking) does not show the same benefit
options.B: Exercise of any intensity has no effect on stroke risk whatsoever
options.C: Only vigorous exercise increases stroke risk
options.D: Light walking provides the greatest protective benefit, more than vigorous exercise

questions.explanation: Moderate to vigorous physical activity is associated with an overall 35% reduction in stroke risk, whereas light exercise such as walking alone does not appear to confer the same degree of protective benefit.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan, Physical Rehabilitation
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 15: Stroke — Risk Factors and Stroke Prevention
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: The maximum weight which can safely be used with skin traction is about:
questions.explanation: Skin traction relies on adhesive or non-adhesive bandages and cannot withstand more than about 4–5 kg without skin damage; skeletal traction is used for heavier forces.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Which position leaves the heels MOST susceptible to pressure damage?

options.D: Prone with feet over the edge

questions.explanation: In supine the heels bear weight on the mattress; offload with pillows under the calves.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Venous leg ulcers are typically located:

options.A: On the lateral border of the foot
options.B: Over the medial malleolus (gaiter area) and are treated with graduated compression
options.D: On the toes with a punched-out margin

questions.explanation: Chronic venous hypertension causes lipodermatosclerosis and ulceration; compression bandaging is the mainstay after excluding arterial disease (ABPI).
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: A patient develops a swollen, shiny, painful hand with stiffness four weeks after plaster removal for a wrist fracture. The most likely diagnosis is:

options.D: Complex regional pain syndrome (reflex sympathetic dystrophy)

questions.explanation: Pain out of proportion, swelling, trophic skin changes and stiffness after immobilisation define CRPS type I; early mobilisation, desensitisation and mirror therapy are used.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: If a patient with SCI on a tilt table becomes dizzy and nauseated, the most appropriate immediate action is to:

options.A: Leave the patient and call a colleague
options.C: Lower the tilt table (or recline the chair) and monitor vital signs

questions.explanation: Pooling of blood in the lower limbs due to loss of sympathetic vasomotor tone; use abdominal binders and stockings and increase angles gradually.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: A ‘huff’ in the forced expiration technique helps clear secretions from:

options.D: Mid- and peripheral airways when done from mid- to low lung volume

questions.explanation: A huff from mid lung volume mobilises secretions in smaller airways; a huff from high volume clears larger central airways.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: To allow adaptation, resistance exercise for the same muscle group is generally performed:

options.D: 2–3 times per week with at least 48 hours between sessions

questions.explanation: Muscle adapts during recovery; ACSM recommends 2–3 days per week for each major muscle group.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: The most specific antibody for systemic lupus erythematosus is:
questions.explanation: ANA is sensitive but not specific; butterfly rash, arthritis, nephritis.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine
